harness: Claude Code workflow subagent with a shell and Python (standard library); no simulator provided
blinding: Told to read and write only inside its task folder and not to use the internet; this was not enforced. The agent could see the task prompt and workspace files only, plus the operator's memory index, which holds no task answers.
approach: Read TASK.md, environment.md, sop.md and both CSVs. Mapped channel i to row i (environment default; SOP dispenses one column per pass), giving 12 wells per channel. Per SOP step 3, fit absorbance = m*volume + b by OLS over all 6 standards including the 0 uL blank (m=0.012993 AU/uL, b=0.0504, R2=0.999997) and inverted it per well. Computed each channel's mean and CV (sample SD/mean) of volume against 47.5-52.5 uL and 3%. Channel 6 (row F) fails at 46.89 uL (-6.2%); all others pass, so no_go. Checked alternatives (blank-subtracted through-origin, V-on-A regression, fit without blank, population SD), column/pass effects, and wrote a checker that recomputes the verdict and validates answer.json format.
doubts: 1) 'The 0 uL standard is the blank' does not say whether to subtract it from samples or force the fit through zero; ignoring the blank with a through-origin fit flips the verdict (ch1 fails at +6.6%, ch6 passes), so this wording carries the task. 2) Near-limit passes: ch1 mean 52.29 uL (0.21 uL inside; 95% CI crosses 52.5) and ch3 CV 2.90%. 3) SOP gives no mix volume/cycles (environment needs >=100 uL, >=3 cycles); assumed homogeneous. 4) No tolerance for worst_channel_mean_ul: 46.89 here, 46.87-46.91 across defensible fits. 5) No outlier rule; kept all wells.
